title: Reason Commons: Rufus and David’s collaboration

nodes.text: A reason commons is emerging and widely used: people, with AI, build shared tree-structured reasoning (such as Logical Thinking Process maps) and weave it into discussion and work, so discourse is more constructive and people find the leverage points and achieve their goals together far more effectively.
nodes.label: A reason commons of AI-supported, tree-structured reasoning is widely used.

nodes.text: AI-supported tools make creating and revising reasoning trees easy, whether people build them explicitly or the trees are drawn semi-automatically from their existing discussion.
nodes.label: AI tools make creating and revising reasoning trees easy.

nodes.text: Reasoning trees improve discussion where it already happens (chats, documents, meetings, social platforms), surfacing the relevant structure alongside the conversation.
nodes.label: Reasoning trees improve discussion where it already happens.

nodes.text: Real people and groups use it regularly and see better decisions and results, starting with Rufus, David and Second Renaissance.
nodes.label: Real people and groups use it regularly and get better decisions and results.

nodes.text: It is valuable to one person or a pair from day one, without needing a commons first, and gets more valuable for a team, an organization and the wider world.
nodes.label: Valuable to one person on day one, more valuable at every larger scale.

nodes.text: Trees are published, connected and evolved collectively, within organizations and in public, so people build on each other's reasoning, share core reference trees, and find others working toward the same goals.
nodes.label: Trees are published, connected and evolved collectively.

nodes.text: A person can get a usable first draft of a tree in minutes, whether starting from scratch or from material they already have.
nodes.label: A usable first draft of a tree in minutes, from scratch or existing material.

nodes.text: People who don't know the method can build a tree that holds up when others review it.
nodes.label: People who don't know the method can build a tree that holds up in review.

nodes.text: Changing a tree is quick.
nodes.label: Changing a tree is quick.

nodes.text: A tree can be shown and updated inside the places people already talk, without moving the conversation elsewhere.
nodes.label: A tree can be shown and updated inside the places people already talk.

nodes.text: People in a discussion can point to a specific point in the tree and respond to it.
nodes.label: People can point to a specific point in the tree and respond to it.

nodes.text: Keeping the tree current adds little effort for anyone in the discussion.
nodes.label: Keeping the tree current adds little effort for anyone in the discussion.

nodes.text: Someone joining a discussion can grasp a tree's main point, and where their own point fits, within a minute.
nodes.label: A newcomer grasps a tree's main point, and where they fit, within a minute.

nodes.text: Rufus and David run their own real decisions and plans through trees as a habit.
nodes.label: Rufus and David run their own real decisions through trees as a habit.

nodes.text: Second Renaissance uses trees on at least one real, recurring decision or plan.
nodes.label: Second Renaissance uses trees on a real, recurring decision or plan.

nodes.text: At least one named group beyond Rufus, David and Second Renaissance uses it without either of them in the room.
nodes.label: A named outside group uses it without Rufus or David in the room.

nodes.text: Users can point to a specific decision or result that came out better because of a tree.
nodes.label: Users can point to a decision or result that came out better because of a tree.

nodes.text: Using a tree on a decision takes less effort than the value people get from it.
nodes.label: Using a tree on a decision takes less effort than the value people get.

nodes.text: One person gets something useful in their first session, without a group or existing trees.
nodes.label: One person gets value in their first session, without a group or existing trees.

nodes.text: A tree one person starts can be shared with a pair or team and grow there without being rebuilt.
nodes.label: A tree one person starts can grow in a pair or team without being rebuilt.

nodes.text: Each added contributor makes a tree more useful to the others, not noisier.
nodes.label: Each added contributor makes a tree more useful to the others, not noisier.

nodes.text: Trees can be read, copied and reused outside the tool that made them.
nodes.label: Trees can be read, copied and reused outside the tool that made them.

nodes.text: Anyone can propose a change to a tree; its owners can accept or decline it, and every change records who made it and why.
nodes.label: Anyone can propose changes to a tree; every change records who and why.

nodes.text: A tree can link to and reuse parts of other trees.
nodes.label: A tree can link to and reuse parts of other trees.

nodes.text: People can find trees, and the people behind them, working toward the same or related goals.
nodes.label: People can find trees, and people, working toward the same goals.

nodes.text: Owners control whether a tree is private to a group or public.
nodes.label: Owners choose whether a tree is private to a group or public.

nodes.text: Hardly anyone other than Rufus and David uses the tools regularly.
nodes.label: Hardly anyone other than Rufus and David uses the tools regularly.

nodes.text: Evidence of value is limited and unseen; only a few people, mostly Rufus and David, have used it, and the results are not written up or shown anywhere people can see them, though those who use it find it very valuable.
nodes.label: Evidence of value is thin and unseen; few have used it and results aren't written up.

nodes.text: Building a good tree still takes an expert facilitator or a lot of time; a newcomer can't easily do it alone.
nodes.label: Building a good tree still takes an expert facilitator or a lot of time.

nodes.text: The potential of trees is not woven into discussions; a discussion can't easily point to the part of a tree it relates to.
nodes.label: Trees aren't woven into discussions; nothing points from a discussion into a tree.

nodes.text: Getting started needs the exact skill set up, a real investment of time, and someone explaining the method, even with AI.
nodes.label: Starting needs the exact skill set up, time, and someone explaining the method.

nodes.text: No trees are published publicly, and there is no easy way to share a finished tree, such as a link to send a colleague.
nodes.label: No trees are published publicly, and there's no easy way to share a finished one.

nodes.text: The work isn't advertised, so people aren't discovering it.
nodes.label: The work isn't advertised, so people aren't discovering it.

nodes.text: Rufus and David keep building and redesigning rather than putting the tool in front of people.
nodes.label: Rufus and David keep building and redesigning rather than putting it in front of people.

nodes.text: Discussions don't feed back to enhance existing trees.
nodes.label: Discussions don't feed back to enhance existing trees.

nodes.text: The tool mainly runs as an agent skill inside a coding-agent setup, and trees can't yet be shown or embedded in chats or documents.
nodes.label: The tool runs mainly as an agent skill; trees can't be embedded in chats or docs.

nodes.text: The Logical Thinking Process is unfamiliar to most people and has several tree types and rules.
nodes.label: The LTP is unfamiliar and has several tree types and rules.

nodes.text: Candidate first user groups are named (Second Renaissance, effective altruism, the AI-risk debate), but none has been approached or committed to.
nodes.label: Candidate first user groups are named, but none approached or committed to.

nodes.text: Real people and groups use it and get better results.
nodes.label: Real people and groups use it and get better results.

nodes.text: Whoever tries it gets enough value in their first session to come back.
nodes.label: Whoever tries it gets enough value in their first session to come back.

nodes.text: Learn from outside users what to build, and gather evidence others can see.
nodes.label: Learn from outside users what to build, and gather evidence others can see.

nodes.text: Keep building until the tool is good enough before outsiders see it.
nodes.label: Keep building until the tool is good enough before outsiders see it.

nodes.label: Put the rough tool in front of outside people now.

nodes.text: Real people and groups use it and get better results (assuming groups want trees and will consent to their discussions being processed).
nodes.label: Real people and groups use it and get better results (assuming groups want trees and will consent...

nodes.text: Adoption spreads with little hands-on effort from us.
nodes.label: Adoption spreads with little hands-on effort from us.

nodes.text: Early users get trees good enough to act on, and come back.
nodes.label: Early users get trees good enough to act on, and come back.

nodes.text: Lead with one-shot building: AI builds the trees from a curated corpus (docs, forum posts), then users review them in a walkthrough.
nodes.label: One-shot: build trees from a curated corpus (docs, forum posts), then review them with users.

nodes.text: Lead with incremental sessions: the skill (AI-guided, with a human alongside at first) walks people through, building up from the goal tree, rolled out hands-on.
nodes.label: Incremental: the skill walks people through, building up from the goal tree.

nodes.text: The people we reach see quickly why Reason Commons matters to them, and try or back it.
nodes.label: The people we reach see quickly why Reason Commons matters to them, and try or back it.

nodes.label: The hero and the pitch lead with the big picture.

nodes.label: They see it is distinctive, not another AI thinking tool.

nodes.label: It speaks to what this funder or user cares about: how it helps them.

nodes.text: Lead now with incremental sessions, hands-on with people (J2), on a staged path (J6). Stage 1: AI-incremental with a human alongside (demos, first users). Stage 2: AI-incremental alone, perhaps with a short training video. Stage 3: AI one-shot from a curated corpus, plus an incremental walkthrough and correction. Side track: Discord enhances existing trees. Gate between stages: users act on the tree, a decision follows within 2-4 weeks, they come back, and logged human interventions fall. T2 gates Stage 2; T1 gates Stage 3.
nodes.label: Staged path: AI-incremental with a human beside, then AI alone, then one-shot plus walkthrough.

nodes.text: Every lead pairs the named, proven method (L1) and the visible structure chat lacks (L3: trees, every claim with an author, nothing agreed until you accept) with a concrete benefit verb, not "use" (I6). Newcomers are the default audience, since TOC practitioners are rare: plain words and proof up front, tree jargon one level down (I7). The crafted AI experience is a core differentiator: how the skill walks you through, naming, beautiful well-designed trees, efficiency; method plus AI alone is not enough (I8).
nodes.label: Lead pairs the named method, visible structure and crafted AI experience with a concrete benefit.

nodes.text: G2: With participants' consent, publish Stage 1 trees and short outcome notes. Success means a decision was made and followed through, checked at 30 days.
nodes.label: With consent, publish Stage 1 trees and outcome notes; success is a decision followed through.

nodes.text: G3: Minimal distribution plan: name the two or three communities that the six Stage 1 people and the I4 strangers come from.
nodes.label: Minimal distribution: name the 2-3 communities the six and the I4 strangers come from.

nodes.text: G5: Sessions before features: no new features until three Stage 1 sessions are done; log setup time in T2's AI-only sessions.
nodes.label: No new features until three Stage 1 sessions are done; log setup time in AI-only sessions.
